figures.caption: Figure 1: Overview of our online Gaussian splatting SLAM system. (a) A frozen streaming foundation model estimates camera intrinsics from the initial RGB frames. (b) Predicted depth and image features support geometric camera tracking through correspondence matching and reprojection error minimization. (c) The Gaussian mapper integrates RGB frames, predicted depth, and estimated poses through keyframe selection, Laplacian-guided Gaussian insertion, and 30-step refinement using RGB and depth losses with keyframe replay.

Figure 2: Ablation on refinement steps per keyframe. Means over the six Oxford Spires sequences. Rendering quality saturates at n{\approx}75 –100 (dashed line). The filled marker is the default n{=}30 used in all main tables.

Table 1: Rendering quality, trajectory accuracy, and efficiency among all datasets. The best results are in bold , and the second-best results are underlined . ATE and \mathrm{RPE}_{t} are reported in centimeters, and \mathrm{RPE}_{R} is reported in degrees. For Photo-SLAM, it fails on the Pumpkin sequence of 7-Scenes and we only use 6 scenes for its average.

Figure 3: Qualitative rendering and depth comparison. One representative sequence is selected from each dataset. For 7-Scenes, TUM-D and Oxford Spires, we show both novel-view RGB rendering and rendered depth; RE10K is shown only in RGB because reference depth is unavailable. The 7-Scenes and TUM-D datasets provide dense reference depth, whereas the Oxford Spires reference depth is sparsely projected from the scanned point cloud. All methods are compared using the same valid-depth mask.

Figure 4: Qualitative trajectory comparison. We visualize one representative sequence from three datasets after trajectory alignment. Our estimated trajectories closely follow the ground truth. Because OTF is designed primarily for novel-view synthesis and estimates poses only for keyframes and held-out views, its trajectory error is computed only over this available pose subset rather than over all input frames.
Table 2: Scale-aligned rendered-depth accuracy. Mean depth L1 error on 7-Scenes, TUM-D, and Oxford Spires. All values are reported in meters; lower is better.

Table 3: Ablation on camera pose estimation over Oxford Spires. For variant C, we use Open3D’s CPU point-to-plane ICP as an unoptimized reference implementation; its runtime does not represent the computational limit of ICP.
Table 4: Geometry-based pose estimation across streaming backbones on Keble College-02.
